items.titleZh: 安东内利称梅赛德斯在美国大奖赛取得进步
items.summaryZh: 安东内利表示，梅赛德斯在美国大奖赛上进一步挖掘了近期升级套件的性能，在奥斯汀带来新的前翼选项。

items.originalTitle: Kimi Antonelli hails "step forward" at United States GP as Mercedes chips away at upgrades
items.summaryEn: Kimi Antonelli says Mercedes made another step in extracting performance from its recent upgrade package at the United States Grand Prix, bringing a new front wing option to Austin.
detailZh: 安东内利称梅赛德斯在美国大奖赛取得进步，车队在逐步消化升级
随着梅赛德斯近期升级让赛车更快但也更难调校到最佳窗口，安东内利认为车队在美国大奖赛练习赛中取得了急需的进展
F1车手积分榜领跑者安东内利认为，梅赛德斯在美国大奖赛上又迈出一步，努力从近期升级套件中挖掘性能。
梅赛德斯来到奥斯汀颇具挑战性的美洲赛道，带来新的前翼选项，以进一步补充两站前在马来西亚引入的重大升级套件。那次初步升级提高了赛车的性能上限，但也让赛车更敏感、更难调校到最佳状态。
在安东内利和乔治·拉塞尔于新加坡站使用不同套件后，如今两人都用上了最新规格，梅赛德斯在奥斯汀从第一节练习到第二节练习的进展表明，W17 仍然很难进入正确的工作窗口。
但当魔法发生时，性能是可以被挖掘出来的，周五安东内利仅落后法拉利在第二节练习领跑的夏尔·勒克莱尔 0.042 秒。
“相比第一节练习，我在车里感觉更好了，”安东内利说。“还有很多工作要做，但这是很好的进步，现在我们会尝试进一步提升。两辆车使用相同套件有帮助，因为我们可以尝试很多不同的东西，也能更好地理解这套套件。”
“自新加坡以来，我们得以分析数据，更好地理解这套套件的需求。我们仍在努力寻找如何让赛车进入正确窗口，但我们一直在向前迈进，我们会看看还能做些什么来进一步提升。”
长距离试跑的初步数据显示，四支顶尖车队实力相当接近，红牛和法拉利或许略领先于梅赛德斯和迈凯伦，这为德克萨斯站的周末增添了悬念。
赛道工程总监安德鲁·肖夫林补充道：“我们第一节练习表现不佳。我们本希望通过两辆车上的升级套件探索更宽的调校窗口，但我们在锁死方面遇到了困难，这在我们单圈工作和长距离试跑中都是很大的限制。”
“我们在进入下午的练习赛前重新调整了赛车，这似乎让我们处于更好的状态。我们的平衡问题减少了，赛车更可预测，圈速也因此有所提升。”
拉塞尔仅获得第五名，落后勒克莱尔零点七秒，因为他没能跑出一个完整的圈——他第一次使用软胎的尝试因超出赛道限制而作废，第二次则因在COTA赛道最快路段S弯中出现巨大甩尾而毁掉。
周六排位赛的故事不仅关乎赛车的极限性能，还关乎如何在严苛的最后一节中让倍耐力的软胎保持活力，因为在排位赛模拟中，随着后轮橡胶开始衰退，多位车手出现了锁死或冲出赛道的情况。
“我认为关键就是在那个连续弯路段保持后胎状态良好，这样你才能在最后一个弯角拥有性能，”车队副领队布拉德利·洛德表示。
布拉德利·洛德，梅赛德斯AMG F1车队副领队
“就是把调校做到位，让赛车能够旋转而不必过度消耗后胎、过度使用油门，如果我们能做到这一点，应该就能处于良好状态。”
理论上，奥斯汀是安东内利锁定首个世界冠军的第一次机会。但这种情况需要这位意大利车手赢得比赛，同时拉塞尔排名第九或更低，并且刘易斯·汉密尔顿排名第五或更低，因此梅赛德斯并没有过度关注这一情形。
洛德指出：“归根结底，基米本周末夺冠意味着车队经历了一场非常糟糕的比赛，因为数学上要求乔治排名第九或更低，这不是我们想要的比赛方式，也不是我们追求的结果。”
“所以，机会非常渺茫，理论上有可能，但实际来说，这不是赛点周末。我们只会努力上场，尽可能多拿积分，然后看看数学上何时能对我们更有利一些。”
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli hails "step forward" at United States GP as Mercedes chips away at upgrades
As Mercedes' recent upgrades made its car quicker but also tougher to get in the sweet spot, Kimi Antonelli felt the squad made much needed progress in United States Grand Prix practice
Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli reckons Mercedes has made another step trying to extract performance from its recent upgrade package at the United States Grand Prix.

Mercedes arrived at Austin's challenging Circuit of the Americas with a new front wing option to further complement its significant upgrade package introduced in Malaysia two races ago. That initial upgrade raised the performance ceiling of the car, but also made it more peaky and harder to optimise.

With both Antonelli and George Russell now on the latest specification after splitting packages in Singapore, Mercedes' progress from first to second practice in Austin suggested the W17 is still difficult to get in the right operating window.
But when the magic happens there is performance to be found, with Antonelli just 0.042s behind Ferrari's FP2 leader Charles Leclerc on Friday.

"I felt better in the car compared to FP1," Antonelli said. "There is still lots of work to do, but it was a good step forward and now we'll try to improve even further. Having both cars on the same package helps, because we can try lots of different stuff and we can have a better understanding of this package.

"Since Singapore we were able to analyse the data and understand better what this package needs. We're still trying to find how to put the car in the right window, but we've been taking steps forward and we'll see what we can do to improve even more."

Initial reads from the long runs suggested all four top teams are fairly evenly matched, with perhaps Red Bull and Ferrari slightly ahead of Mercedes and McLaren, setting up an intriguing weekend in Texas.

Trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin added: "We didn’t have a good first session. We were looking to explore a wider set-up window with the update package on both cars, but we were struggling with locking, which was a big limitation in both our single-lap work and the long runs.

"We repositioned the cars going into the afternoon session and that seems to have put us in a better place. We had fewer balance issues, the car was more predictable, and the lap times improved as a result."

Russell only managed fifth, seven tenths behind Leclerc, after not getting a proper lap in - his first soft tyre effort scratched for exceeding track limits and his second ruined by a huge snap through the fastest portion of COTA's Esses.

The story of Saturday qualifying will not just be about ultimate car performance, but also about keeping Pirelli's soft tyres alive through the demanding final sector, with several drivers locking up or going off the track as the rear rubber started fading in qualifying simulations.
"I think it's just all about keeping the rear tyres in good shape through that twisty bit so that you've got the performance in the last corner," said deputy team principal Bradley Lord.
Bradley Lord, Deputy Team Principal, Mercedes AMG F1 Team

"It's just getting the set-up in the right place and getting the car able to rotate without needing to overuse the rear tyres, overuse the throttle and if we can do that then we should be in good shape."

Austin is theoretically the first opportunity for Antonelli to seal his maiden world championship. But as that would involve the Italian winning the race with Russell finishing ninth or lower - and Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth or lower - it's not a scenario Mercedes is overly preoccupied with.

"Ultimately, for Kimi to win this weekend it means the team's had a really bad race, because the maths say George needs to be ninth or below, and that isn't how we want to go racing and the result we're aiming for," Lord pointed out.

"So, it's a very minimal chance, it's theoretically possible, but in practical terms, this isn't the match point weekend. We'll just try and get out there, get as many points as possible and then see when the maths start to come towards us a little bit more."

items.titleZh: 美国大奖赛竞争开放 法拉利红牛梅赛德斯各有强弱
items.summaryZh: 根据奥斯汀开局表现，F1美国大奖赛可能演变为多支车队争胜，法拉利、红牛和梅赛德斯单圈差距不到0.2秒，但各自在不同路段有强有弱。
items.originalTitle: F1's wide-open US GP fight explained
items.summaryEn: Based on how the top teams have started at Austin, F1's United States Grand Prix looks poised to be a multi-team fight for victory, with Ferrari, Red Bull and Mercedes separated by less than two tenths on single-lap pace but each strong and weak in different parts of the track.
detailZh: 根据各顶尖车队在奥斯汀的开局表现，F1美国大奖赛看起来将是一场多支车队争夺胜利的较量。
以下是关于竞争格局的早期线索，单圈速度与长距离速度的趋势呈现出非常不同的画面。
领先赛车各有不同强项，加上奥斯汀赛道弯道速度范围很广、考验赛车各个方面，这意味着在单圈速度上相差不到0.2秒的法拉利、红牛和梅赛德斯，都在赛道的不同路段各有出色和挣扎之处。
领跑者夏尔·勒克莱尔在慢弯最强。他在1号弯保持了最高的最低速度，在12号弯追平了基米·安东内利的最佳值，并在11号发夹弯晚刹车且没有影响出弯。他往往是最早重新踩下油门的车手。
在高速路段，勒克莱尔在6-7号弯最快，在马克斯·维斯塔潘收油的地方保持了部分油门——不过，快速弯中的情况有时会因能量部署的差异而变得模糊。和往常一样，法拉利在直道上损失了显著的时间——相对于维斯塔潘刚刚超过0.6秒。
维斯塔潘的红牛在直道上非常强大，一旦速度稳定下来，比勒克莱尔快了约0.6秒，相比梅赛德斯也快了略多于0.1秒。这一特性也让他在起跑/终点直道上的单圈开局很强。他在刹车方面全力投入，制动力很强，但在慢弯出弯时往往更晚给油，这种做法在20号弯得到了回报，他在那里出弯很强。
对维斯塔潘来说，红牛最欠缺的地方在相当不错的一天之后变得很明显，这让这位四届F1世界冠军寻求更精细的平衡，而非任何 drastic 的改动。
当被 The Race 问及是否有突出的领域需要在一夜之间改进时，红牛技术总监皮埃尔·瓦什的判断是：“目前我们显然专注于低速性能。”
“低速对我们来说是关键。”
前面提到的维斯塔潘偏好稍早但更重地刹车，以优先保证良好出弯，这一点在整圈中都很明显，但除了20号弯之外，由于红牛赛车似乎缺乏旋转，这并没有真正体现在圈速上。
维斯塔潘的1号弯是前三名中最差的。尽管他刹车最早，但回到全油门却最慢——因为他需要处理一些车轮打滑——并且从比勒克莱尔快略超过0.1秒变成了落后0.25秒。
12号弯是他的另一个大损失，又大约0.2秒。尽管再次刹车更早，维斯塔潘在最初开始打方向入弯时没有得到他需要的响应，跑得稍微偏深，使他的最低速度比勒克莱尔和安东内利低了10公里/小时。
红牛赛车在这里的刹车区遇到颠簸时可能不够服帖，这导致维斯塔潘刹车稍早，入弯时不够凌厉或自信，出弯也不够稳定。
“找到正确的平衡比预期更困难，”瓦赫承认。
安东内利的梅赛德斯赛车表现更为均衡：直道上比法拉利快，但未达到红牛水平，不过在接近发夹弯时展现出良好速度。这可能反映了部署策略上的差异。
他在8-9号弯、15号弯和12号弯表现强劲，但在几个弯角的出弯处有所损失。
迈凯伦的单圈速度在成绩表上也毫无亮点，兰多·诺里斯是其二练中较快的车手，但落后榜首1.082秒。不过，这个圈速是用硬胎做出的，因为他不得不中止了两次排位模拟圈。
第一次是因为在9号弯弯心出现打滑，可能是受到前方乔治·拉塞尔的梅赛德斯赛车造成的乱流影响。他的第二圈使用软胎倍耐力，此时已过最佳状态，在15号弯锁死后被放弃。
迈凯伦首席技术官罗布·马歇尔表示：“我们在二练中也做出了紫色（最快赛段成绩），只是没能完成那一圈。在犯错之前，那一圈是有竞争力的。”
“从这里往前看，我们真的必须相当乐观。”
他做出这个第一赛段时间时，这是当时最快的第一赛段时间，尽管后来被维斯塔潘超越，但只差了0.015秒——而且这比法拉利或梅赛德斯取得的任何成绩都要快。
从原始数据来看，诺里斯的迈凯伦在第二次练习赛的长距离平均圈速上最快，但由于多种原因，情况令人困惑。
交通状况影响了几位车手的长距离测试，而且三种轮胎配方都被使用过，因此很难将诺里斯用耐用硬胎跑出的九圈与维斯塔潘用软胎跑出的十一圈进行对比。
但诺里斯强劲的长距离表现印证了迈凯伦比第二次练习赛成绩所显示的更强大。
倍耐力预计硬胎“在决定比赛策略方面只会发挥有限的作用”，最有可能采用软胎和中性胎的一停策略。
维斯塔潘的软胎表现令人印象深刻地出色，圈速稳定，相比勒克莱尔的轮胎衰减更小。
队友伊萨克·哈贾尔显然没有那么适应。他全天都在与过热的前胎作斗争；谈到自己的软胎圈时，他说“简直就是一场灾难”。
“车根本没法开，前部严重失去抓地力。我们需要查一查，因为这不正常，为什么一圈之内就有这么大的衰减。”
哈贾尔表示，他的轮胎在高速弯里“完全废了”。红牛的瓦赫说，这是造成差异的关键，他表示哈贾尔和维斯塔潘在调校上差距不大。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿、乔治·拉塞尔、奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里和哈贾尔似乎都在周末开始时比各自队友慢了一步。
汉密尔顿表示，他“在调校上尝试了不同方向，但我在车里不舒服，尤其是在颠簸路段”，而皮亚斯特里用软胎的长距离节奏似乎急剧下滑。
随着各车队在一夜之间吸取经验并调整调校和能量部署模式，这一局面可能会改变，但目前四支车队看起来都在奥斯汀的争夺行列中。
detailEn: Formula 1's United States Grand Prix looks poised to be a multi-team fight for victory based on how the top four teams have started at Austin.
Here are the early clues about the pecking order, with single-lap and long-run pace trends painting very different pictures.

The combination of the varying strengths of the leading cars and the wide range of corner speeds of the Austin circuit that tests every facet of a car means that Ferrari, Red Bull and Mercedes, which were separated by less than two tenths on single-lap pace, all excelled and struggled at different parts of the track.

Pacesetter Charles Leclerc was strongest in the slow corners. He carried the highest minimum speed at Turn 1, matched Kimi Antonelli's best at Turn 12, and braked late for the Turn 11 hairpin without compromising his exit. He was often first back on the throttle.

In the high-speed sections, Leclerc was quickest through Turns 6-7, keeping part-throttle where Max Verstappen lifted - however, at times the picture in the fast corners was muddied by deployment variations. As always, the Ferrari lost significant time on the straights - just over six tenths relative to Verstappen.

Verstappen's Red Bull was mighty on the straights, gaining around six tenths on Leclerc once the speeds had settled, and a little over a tenth compared to the Mercedes. That characteristic also gave him a strong start to the lap down the start/finish straight. He was committed on the brakes in terms of stopping power, but was often later on the throttle at slow-corner exits, with that approach paying off at Turn 20, where he had a strong exit.
Where Red Bull is lacking most for Verstappen was obvious after a pretty good day left the four-time F1 world champion seeking a finer balance rather than anything drastic.

"It's clearly the low-speed performance that we are focused on at the moment," was Red Bull technical director Pierre Wache's verdict when asked by The Race if there was a standout area to improve overnight.
"Low speed is the key for us."

That aforementioned Verstappen preference for braking slightly earlier, but harder, to prioritise a good exit was clear throughout the lap but, other than at Turn 20, it did not really manifest in laptime due to the Red Bull seemingly lacking rotation.

Verstappen's Turn 1 was the worst of the top three. Despite braking earliest he was slowest back to full throttle - due to some wheelspin he had to manage - and swung from just over a tenth up on Leclerc to 0.25s behind.

Turn 12 was his other big loss, around 0.2s again. Despite again braking earlier, Verstappen did not have the response he needed when he initially started applying steering lock into the corner and ran a little deep, dropping his minimum speed 10km/h below Leclerc's and Antonelli's.

It's possible the Red Bull is not quite as compliant on the bumps in the braking zones here, which is contributing to Verstappen braking slightly earlier and not being as attacking or as confident on entry, or as steady on exit.
"Finding the right balance was more difficult than expected," Wache admitted.

Antonelli's Mercedes had a more balanced performance profile: quicker on the straights than the Ferrari but not at Red Bull level, but showing good speed on the approach to the hairpin. Potentially, that reflected differences in deployment.
He was strong in Turns 8-9, Turn 15 and Turn 12, but did lose out in several corners on the exits.

McLaren's single-lap pace also looked nowhere on the timesheets, with Lando Norris the faster of its drivers in FP2 but 1.082s off the pace. However, this time was set on hards as he had to abort both of his qualifying simulation laps.

The first was because of a snap mid-corner at Turn 9, possibly the result of running in turbulent air caused by George Russell's Mercedes ahead. His second lap, on soft Pirellis now past their best, was abandoned after a lockup at Turn 15.

"We set a purple [fastest sector time] in FP2 as well, we just didn't finish the lap," said McLaren chief technical officer Rob Marshall. "It was a competitive lap up until the point where we made a mistake.
"Going forward from here we've got to be quite optimistic really."
That first sector time was the fastest at the time he set it, and although it was eclipsed by Verstappen that was only by 0.015s - and it was faster than anything achieved by Ferrari or Mercedes.
On the raw numbers, Norris's McLaren was fastest on the long-run averages in FP2, but it's a confusing picture for a number of reasons.

Traffic affected a number of drivers' long runs and all three tyre compounds were used, so it's tricky to compare a nine-lap Norris run on durable hards to Verstappen's 11-lap soft-tyre run, for example.
But Norris's strong long run backs up McLaren looking stronger than the FP2 result suggested.
Pirelli expects the hard tyre to "play only a limited role in defining race strategies", with a one-stop using the softs and mediums most likely.
Verstappen's soft tyres held up impressively well with consistent laptimes and less of a drop-off compared to Leclerc's.
Team-mate Isack Hadjar was clearly not as comfortable. He struggled with overheating front tyres all day; "it's just a disaster" he said of his soft tyre lap.
"It was just undriveable, and I was losing the front end massively. We need to have a look because that's not normal, why there is so much deg on one lap."
Hadjar said his tyres were "completely killed" in the high-speed corners. Red Bull's Wache said this was key to the difference as he said Hadjar and Verstappen weren't far apart on set-up.
Lewis Hamilton, George Russell, Oscar Piastri and Hadjar all appear to have started the weekend a step behind their respective team-mates.

Hamilton said he "tried a different direction with the set-up, but I wasn't comfortable in the car, especially over the bumps", while Piastri's long run pace on the softs appeared to sharply tail off.
That picture may alter as teams learn overnight lessons and change set-up and deployment patterns, but right now all four teams look like they are in the hunt at Austin.
keyPointsZh: 勒克莱尔在慢弯最强：1号弯最低速度最高，12号弯与安东内利的最佳值持平，11号发夹弯刹车晚且未影响出弯。
勒克莱尔在6至7号弯的高速路段最快，在马克斯·维斯塔潘收油处保持部分油门。
法拉利在直道上相对维斯塔潘损失超过0.6秒。
keyPointsEn: Leclerc was strongest in the slow corners: he carried the highest minimum speed at Turn 1, matched Antonelli's best at Turn 12, and braked late for the Turn 11 hairpin without compromising his exit.
Leclerc was quickest through the high-speed Turns 6-7, keeping part-throttle where Max Verstappen lifted.
Ferrari lost just over six tenths relative to Verstappen on the straights.

items.titleZh: 威廉姆斯美国站周五异常：为2027年研发牺牲练习赛
items.summaryZh: 威廉姆斯在美国大奖赛周五练习赛中表现异常，最快赛车落后凯迪拉克且距领先者8.1秒，FP1主要为2027年研发进行空气动力学测试。
items.originalTitle: What was behind one F1 team's strangest day of 2026
items.summaryEn: Williams had an unusual Friday at the United States Grand Prix, with its fastest car slower than Cadillac and 8.1 seconds off the pace, as FP1 was largely devoted to aerodynamic testing for 2027 development.
detailZh: 威廉姆斯在美国大奖赛经历了一个奇怪的周五，练习赛结束时其最快的F1赛车比凯迪拉克还慢，距领先者8.1秒。
亚历山大·阿尔本在FP2中夸张地排名垫底（正如他在FP1中一样），但车队的真实速度仍然令人失望，卡洛斯·塞恩斯甚至排在瓦尔特利·博塔斯驾驶的凯迪拉克之后。
一次赛道限制导致的圈速删除是阿尔本特别异常差距的原因，而2026年最奇怪的周五部分是因为威廉姆斯在FP1中牺牲了常规的周末工作，以帮助2027年的研发。
这意味着FP1用硬胎进行空气动力学测试，随后是短暂的中性胎运行，威廉姆斯首席赛道工程师保罗·威廉姆斯表示，车队“在周末表现与长期学习之间做了平衡”，因为“这条赛道非常适合收集空气动力学数据”。
塞恩斯表示：“我们决定把第一节练习的时间投入到一条我们知道会表现不佳的赛道上，以了解如何基本上为赛车绘制图谱，从而尽可能多地从今年的赛车中学习，为明年的赛车做准备。”
“我们知道今年的赛车在这样的赛道上有很多弱点，我们希望确保理解它，并绘制图谱，以便明年在风洞中把它做对。”
随后第二节练习的重点是更标准的周五计划，只是更加强调高油量运行，因为威廉姆斯知道自己的单圈速度无论如何都可能不足——尽管其长距离速度在中游车队中也显得疲软。
美洲赛道是一条严苛的赛道，因为其布局包含中高速弯道、长时间弯角和颠簸的重刹车区。
这暴露了威廉姆斯车队近年来的许多潜在弱点，以及其2026款赛车的具体短板。
在第二节练习赛中，就在塞恩斯抱怨赛车一团糟、他对车尾毫无信心之后不久，阿尔本报告称他在制动时毫无信心。
“当你没有下压力时，你会在制动或高速时受苦，”塞恩斯说。
“我们知道今年我们的赛车缺乏大量下压力，尤其是当赛道颠簸、高速、高温、刮风的时候——就像在COTA那样——唯一能救你的就是下压力，而这正是我们今年赛车上所没有的。
“所以我们正在努力，我们已为艰难的周末做好准备，不要期待奇迹，但至少我们正投入精力，尽可能多地为明年学习。”
detailEn: Williams had a peculiar Friday at the United States Grand Prix as it ended practice with its fastest Formula 1 car slower than Cadillac and the other 8.1 seconds off the pace.
Alex Albon was an exaggerated slowest in FP2 (just as he was in FP1) but the team's real pace was still disappointing, with Carlos Sainz even behind Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac.

A track-limits deletion was behind Albon's particularly unusual deficit and the strangest Friday of 2026 was partly down to Williams sacrificing typical in-weekend work for 2027 development help in FP1.

This meant aero testing on hards in FP1 followed by a short medium-tyre run, as Williams chief trackside engineer Paul Williams said the team had "balanced off performance for this weekend versus long-term learning" because "this track's very good for aero data collection".

Sainz said: "We decided to invest FP1 on a track that we knew we were going to be weak [on] to understand how to basically map the car in order to learn from this year's car as much as possible for next year's car.
"We know we have a lot of weaknesses on this year's car on a track like this and we want to make sure we understand it and we map it to try and get it right next year in the windtunnel."

Then the focus in FP2 was a more standard Friday plan just with a heavier emphasis on high-fuel running as Williams knows its one-lap pace is likely to be lacking anyway - although its long-run pace looked weak in the midfield too.
The Circuit of the Americas is a punishing track as its layout comprises a mix of medium- and high-speed sweeps, long-duration corners, and bumpy heavy braking zones.
This exposes a lot of Williams's underlying weaknesses of recent years and the specific shortcomings of its 2026 car.
In FP2, shortly after Sainz complained the car was a mess and he had no confidence in the rear, Albon reported zero confidence under braking.
"When you have no downforce you're going to suffer either on braking or on high speed," said Sainz.

"We know this year we lack a lot of downforce in the car and especially when it gets bumpy, when it gets high speed, when it gets hot, when it gets windy - like it gets in COTA - the only thing that saves you is downforce and that's what we don't have on this year's car.
"So we're working on it, we are braced for a tough weekend, don't expect any miracles, but at least we are investing in learning as much as possible for next year."
keyPointsZh: 阿尔本在FP2排名垫底，部分原因是赛道限制导致圈速被删除
塞恩斯在FP2中甚至排在博塔斯驾驶的凯迪拉克之后
威廉姆斯首席赛道工程师保罗·威廉姆斯表示，车队在周末表现与长期学习之间做了平衡，因为这条赛道非常适合收集空气动力学数据
keyPointsEn: Albon was slowest in FP2, partly because a track-limits deletion removed his lap time.
Sainz was even behind Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac in FP2.
Williams chief trackside engineer Paul Williams said the team balanced off performance for this weekend versus long-term learning because this track is very good for aero data collection.
